claims.text: Adding approximately 3–5 at% Al to a refractory HEA will trigger formation of nanoscale coherent B2-ordered precipitates.
The B2 precipitates will impede dislocation motion at elevated temperatures.
The Al addition will enhance high-temperature strength, including creep resistance.
The Al addition will reduce the overall alloy density.
The Al addition will preserve room-temperature mechanical performance.
The initial material is a refractory HEA based on high-melting-point elements such as Mo, Nb, Ta, and W.
The initial alloy has a single-phase microstructure without secondary precipitates.
A suitable thermomechanical treatment after adding Al will produce a uniform distribution of fine B2 precipitates.
The intended strengthening effect should occur during creep or tensile loading at 1100–1200°C.
Coherent B2 precipitates act as barriers to both dislocation glide and dislocation climb at high temperature.
Blocking dislocation glide and climb will increase creep resistance and high-temperature yield strength.
A low volume fraction and fine distribution of precipitates will minimize loss of room-temperature ductility.
Because Al has relatively low density, its addition will slightly reduce overall alloy density.
Compared with an identically processed alloy without Al, the Al-modified alloy will show approximately 20–50% higher high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance.
Room-temperature mechanical properties will remain essentially unchanged or improve slightly relative to the no-Al baseline.
The strengthening effect requires Al content to remain below the level at which excessive brittle intermetallic networks form.
The strengthening effect depends on processing that maintains a coherent precipitate morphology and suitable precipitate size and distribution.

The hypothesis is falsified if the Al-containing material fails to achieve at least approximately 20% improvement in high-temperature strength, degrades room-temperature properties, or does not contain the expected nanoscale precipitates.
